Daily Devotional

September 19

26 If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain. (James 1:26 KJV)

God is telling us through James, that no matter how religious a man seems, if he can not control his tongue (the words that he speaks), then his religion is not true religion. You can tell by the words that men speak, as to what is really in their hearts, as out of the heart man speaks (Matthew 12:34). If you listen to a person talk long enough, you will get a pretty good idea as to how their hearts are toward God. Our talk and actions do indicate just how much we are living for Christ.

James says that no man can tame the tongue (James 3:8). That is so true in our own abilities, so we have to walk in the spirit, and let Jesus live through us before we ever have a chance to tame our tongues, and to only speak in accordance with the Word of God. Under stress a person tends to let what is in their hearts come out of their mouths. This sure lets us know that the words we speak are either bringing life or death to us (Proverbs 18:21). Every word you speak is working power in the spiritual realm, so be careful what you say, as you will eat the fruit of your mouth. Jesus said that we would be held accountable for every idle word that we speak (Matthew 12:36), so watch your words.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

"For the kids it's really important to see that they're not alone and that all these kids have the same history, and they're all adopted and they're all from the same country," Marielle said.

"It's really nice to see them all together and to talk to each other about experiences -- with their hair and with their skin -- and they're all the same people with the same mindset, so it's really fun for the kids and for us, as well."

The couple encourages their children to embrace their American origins, celebrating Thanksgiving each year with other families who adopted children from the United States. Their children stand out in Het Gooi, a village about 30 miles (50 kilometers) from Amsterdam. "They're famous here, where we live, because it's a really white society," Marielle said.
